newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast crude prices ease as July talk picks up.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast crude prices ease as July talk picks up.

text.p: U.S. West Coast oil prices slid Thursday in line with weakening domestic crude markets amid inactive trade, players said.
West Coast players said today's quiet local trade was typical for the beginning of the month as most refiners held meetings to figure out their supply needs.
Crude oil futures for July delivery dropped 46 cents a barrel, indicating a downward price trend according to experts who chart market values.
Traders also are concerned about oversupply, following a report by the American Petroleum Petroleum Tuesday that crude inventories rose a sharp 8.4 million barrels last week.
Tosco Corp, normally a buyer, was looking to sell a full cargo of regional benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) Thursday at $2.00 under WTI.
With Tosco cutting runs of crude oil the last two weeks, the company's refineries have held off using an ANS cargo, and a full cargo of Cano Limon.
Tosco is also offering the Cano Limon, which it bought for $3.10 a barrel under June WTI from Ecopetrol last month, traders said.
Buyers expect the next ANS cargo to sell wider than $2.25 a barrel off July WTI.
ANS outright prices eased 50 cents a barrel on the day in line with weaker futures and cash WTI markets.
Ultramar will bring in cargoes of Oriente and Peruvian Laredo crude for June and July, traders said.
